text:
leah: Heads-up — onboarding sampleapp hit a mismatch between embeddings/rerank when the batching helper retries. Rerank scores were paired to the wrong queries.

jon: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro?

leah: Yep. Repro is the sampleapp using batch helper + the SDK auto-retry on HTTP 502. When retry happens we see the request body going out in chunks, but the helper concat step doesn't preserve the original item order. Example payload we send (simplified):
```json
{
  "requests": [
    {"qid": "q-A", "vector": [0.12, 0.03, 0.88]},
    {"qid": "q-B", "vector": [0.11, 0.04, 0.79]},
    {"qid": "q-C", "vector": [0.01, 0.99, 0.02]}
  ]
}
```
And the backend replies with rerank scores matching the payload order. If the helper splits into batches [q-A,q-B] + [q-C] then retries the first batch, we sometimes see the final assembled request as [q-B,q-A,q-C] (order changed) — so scores get assigned to the wrong qid.

maya: That sounds like a mutation during concat rather than stable reassembly. Which SDKs show this?

leah: Node sampleapp exhibits it consistently with the official batch helper. Python flow seems less frequent but reproducible if you enable async concurrency.

sam: Could be a race in the helper's array splicing when retries re-insert items. Quick workaround: include an explicit id per item (you already have qid) and when the response comes back, map scores by qid instead of assuming index alignment.

jon: We should fix the helper so it never relies on positional alignment. Also need parity across SDKs: Node and Python helpers must behave the same on retry. I'll open a ticket.

leah: For folks debugging: check whether your client side does any in-place sort or uses Object.keys order vs stable array. I found a tiny repro where `Array.prototype.splice` + Promise.all reordering caused the swap.

maya: Filed DE-7892 for helper reassembly bug, assigned to eng-runtime. Adding test cases for retry + partial success + reorder.

devex-bot: Incident DE-7892 created and linked to #eng-runtime.

sam: Short-term patch idea: helper should attach a monotonic sequence field `_batch_idx` and use that to reassemble even if the list gets re-ordered by concurrency. Then publish a patched minor release for both SDKs.

jon: Agree. Also add an integration test that simulates 502 and partial retries with randomized reorder to catch flakiness.

leah: For anyone blocked: quick fix in sampleapp is to map results by `qid` instead of relying on array index. I'll send a tiny PR to docs with that pattern.

maya: Thx. Can someone add a note to the onboarding checklist: "always include stable ids when using embed/rerank batching"?

jon: Added to onboarding checklist + example code snippet.

leah: Thanks all — marking this thread resolved for the sampleapp case. Will follow DE-7892 for the helper patch. :thumbsup:
